name: Bashir Shihab II
note: Emir of Mount Lebanon under Ottoman suzerainty; infobox gives September 1789 to October 1840 (other sources: 1788). End = firman of 8 Oct 1840 replacing him; he was then exiled.

name: Bashir Shihab III (Bashir Qasim)
note: Appointed by Sultan Abdulmejid I after Bashir II (other sources: 3 Sep 1840; Wikipedia's Bashir III article says 1841-1842). Besieged at Deir al-Qamar in Oct 1841; sultan withdrew his appointment in Jan 1842 and he went to Constantinople. Last Shihab emir.

name: Omar Pasha (Ottoman direct rule)
note: Ottoman-appointed ruler of Mount Lebanon after Bashir III, a Sunni of Austrian origin, rejected by most Christians. Exact start and end dates not given in sources read; end inferred from the 7 Dec 1842 decision to partition Mount Lebanon.

name: Haydar Abu'l-Lama
note: Christian qaimaqam (northern district). Double Qaimaqamate; start year per Double Qaim-Maqamate article (the decision to partition was taken 7 Dec 1842).

name: Bashir Ahmad Abu'l-Lama
note: Christian qaimaqam (northern district). Years only in source.

name: Hassan Abu'l-Lama
note: Christian qaimaqam (northern district). Years only in source.

name: Ahmad Arslan
note: Druze qaimaqam (southern district). Years only in source.

name: Amin Arslan
note: Druze qaimaqam (southern district). Years only in source.

name: Muhammad Arslan
note: Druze qaimaqam (southern district). Years only in source; the system ended with the Reglement Organique of 9 Jun 1861.

name: Youssef Bey Karam
note: Christian qaimaqam (northern district), named by Fuad Pasha; term ended with the Mutasarrifate. Infobox of his article gives 17 Nov 1860 to 9 Jun 1861.

name: Daoud Pasha (Garabet Artin Davoudian)
note: First mutasarrif; Armenian Catholic. Appointed under the Protocol of 9 Jun 1861 and imperial decree of 17 Jul 1861; term renewed 1864. End month inferred from successor's decrees of 5 and 11 Jun 1868.

name: Franko Pasha (Nasri Franco Coussa)
note: Melkite Greek Catholic. Imperial decrees of 5 and 11 Jun 1868; term fixed for ten years by protocol of 27 Jul 1868; died 2 Feb 1873 in office.

name: Administrative Council of Mount Lebanon
note: Council asked to assume the governor's duties during the interregnum after Franko's death (Akarli). Rustem was appointed by decrees of Feb 1873; end date = protocol ratifying him.

name: Rustem Pasha (Rustem Mariani)
note: Third mutasarrif; ratified by protocol of 22 Apr 1873 for ten years (decrees Feb 1873). End month inferred from successor's appointment of 8-17 May 1883.

name: Wassa Pasha (Pashko Vasa)
note: Albanian Catholic. Protocol of 8 May 1883 and decrees of 10-17 May 1883; died in office 26 Jun 1892 (Wikipedia's Pashko Vasa article says appointed 18 Jun 1882 and died 29 Jun 1892).

name: Administrative Council of Mount Lebanon
note: Interregnum after Vasa's death; Council assumed the governor's responsibilities (Akarli). End date = protocol appointing Naum.

name: Naum Pasha (Naum Coussa Tutunju)
note: Protocol of 15 Aug 1892 and decree of 17 Aug 1892; extended five years by protocol of 14 Aug 1897. End = date of successor's decree (2 Oct 1902); he returned to Istanbul in 1902.

name: Muzaffer Pasha (Wladyslaw Czajkowski)
note: Protocol of 2 Sep 1902 and decree of 2 Oct 1902; died in office 28 Jun 1907.

name: Yusuf Franko Pasha (Yusuf Coussa)
note: Protocol of 8 Jul 1907 and decree of 9 Jul 1907. End date inferred from successor's decree of 23 Dec 1912.

name: Ohannes Pasha (Ohannes Kouyoumdjian)
note: Protocol and decree of 23 Dec 1912 (arrived Jan 1913); resigned 5 Jun 1915 under Jamal Pasha. Last Christian mutasarrif. Protocols formally abrogated by Istanbul on 11 Jul 1915.

name: Ali Munif Bey
note: Ottoman governor of Mount Lebanon (autonomous regime no longer in force); then governor of Beirut. Gap Jun-Sep 1915 under direct military control (Jamal Pasha); not dated in sources read.

name: Ismail Haqqi Bey
note: Ottoman governor of Mount Lebanon, replaced Ali Munif; start inferred from Ali Munif's end date, end from Mumtaz Bey's start (Wikipedia's Mutasarrifate article says 1917-1918 and that Mumtaz began 31 Jul 1918).

name: Mumtaz Bey
note: Last Ottoman governor of Mount Lebanon (other sources: took office 31 Jul 1918); left Baabda on 30 Sep 1918 as the Ottoman army retreated.

name: Zulufli Ali Pasha
note: Wali of Beirut (Beirut Vilayet, created 1888 from the Syria Vilayet). Month-level dates from the Turkish Wikipedia list. Source gives December 1887 as start.

note: Wali of Beirut (Beirut Vilayet, created 1888 from the Syria Vilayet). Month-level dates from the Turkish Wikipedia list. Akarli says Ali Munif was governor of Beirut from 15 May 1916 and Ismail Haqqi replaced him late in the war, which conflicts with this list.

name: Muftuzade Ismail Hakki Bey
note: Wali of Beirut (Beirut Vilayet, created 1888 from the Syria Vilayet). Month-level dates from the Turkish Wikipedia list. May be the same Ismail Haqqi Bey who governed Mount Lebanon 1916-18 (Akarli); not verified.

name: Francois Georges-Picot
note: French High Commissioner for Palestine and Syria (wartime civil representative, distinct from the Mandate High Commissioner Gouraud from Oct 1919). Years only in source.

name: Marie Antoine Philpin de Piepape
note: Chief Administrator of OETA North, renamed OETA West in Dec 1918 (Beirut, Mount Lebanon, Latakia). Allenby announced OETA on 23 Oct 1918.

name: Jules Camille Hamelin
note: Chief Administrator, OETA West.

name: Francois Georges Barb
note: Chief Administrator, OETA West until the State of Greater Lebanon was proclaimed on 1 Sep 1920. Name spelled as in the Wikipedia list; spelling not cross-checked.
